thread:
Marta G: Alert: kv-shard-12 hit two OOMs during the canary spike (09:14). Logs show increasing live set and a slow GC pause. Uploaded pprofs to s3://redwood/debug/kv/4987654321.tgz
Rex H: Can you paste the short pprof top? wondering if Put()/applyBatch are top allocators.
Marta G: top alloc_space:
```
pprof: top
25MB  runtime.mallocgc
14MB  github.com/redwood/runtime/kv.(*Shard).applyBatch
6MB   github.com/redwood/runtime/cache.newEntry
```
Sofia N: Immediate mitigation: enable a 70% soft-heap cap + enable ephemeral eviction TTL=60s on the shard. I can flip it now on canary. Anyone object?
Lee C: Go for it. Also, flagging recurring-pattern since similar OOMs occurred after bulk import last month. Add to postmortem watchlist.
devops-bot: Created INF-5188: "kv-shard-12 OOM - profiling + soft-cap" (assigned: Rex H) :white_check_mark:
Rex H: I'm taking profiling diffs. Plan: capture at t0/t+10/t+30; run `go tool pprof -inuse_space -alloc_space` and diff. Will post script in INF-5188. ETA tomorrow morning.
Marta G: Also want to run a GOGC experiment (baseline -> 90 -> 150) to see if earlier GC reduces fragmentation spike. Sofia, can you own the GC run and collect latency/CPU tradeoffs?
Sofia N: Yep. I'll run controlled runs on a small canary subset and log metrics. Report due: 2026-03-29.
Lee C: Long-term: add per-shard fragmentation ratio metric (contiguous_free / total_alloc). Owner candidate: Rex for schema, Lee for console. Target prototype next sprint.
Marta G: Quick action recap to add to postmortem follow-ups doc:
- A1: Heap snapshots + diff script (owner: Rex H) 1 due: 2026-03-28
- A2: Soft-heap cap + ephemeral eviction (owner: Sofia N) 1 due: 2026-03-25
- A3: GOGC experiment + perf report (owner: Sofia N) 1 due: 2026-03-29
- A4: Frag metric prototype + dashboard mock (owners: Rex H / Lee C) 1 due: 2026-04-03
Rex H: Will post initial diffs to INF-5188 and attach links here. Please put follow-up notes in the ticket.
Sofia N: Soft-cap applied to canary at 09:30, evict_count=64 in 18m, no new OOMs so far.
Marta G: Thanks team. We'll review INF-5188 in the postmortem follow-up sync next week.
